messages:
mike: heads-up: thinking about a 'bandwidth shepherd' — scheduler to smooth host<->GPU DMA so small interactive evicts don't get stuck behind big batch drains.
anya: nice. we've seen p99 spikes during nightly batch drains. how do you plan to signal urgency?
mike: allocator emits a tiny hint: urgency=(interactive|normal|batch), est_bytes, prefetch_ok. runtime schedules transfers respecting per-tenant windows.
kai: fairness question: token-bucket per tenant or global fair-queue? per-tenant seems safer for noisy neighbor.
ravi: agreed per-tenant + pool caps. also topology-aware multiplier: cross-NUMA transfers cost more. I'll prototype a sysfs probe.
mike: tradeoff: coalescing bulk transfers improves throughput but harms tail. scheduler should avoid coalescing if an interactive item is pending.
anya: need telemetry before tuning: inflight_pcie_bytes, queued_by_urgency, avg_transfer_size, p99_offload_latency. I'll add panels.
kai: incremental plan: (1) add hint to allocator (no-op), (2) telemetry hooks, (3) tenant token-buckets + interactive bypass, (4) microbench mixed pattern.
ravi: microbench pattern suggestion: 40% seq64 interactive, 60% seq2048 batch. sweep window sizes and watch p95/p99.
deploy-bot: infra-experiments/bandwidth-shepherd canary started (no-prod).
mike: thanks — I'll write a short RFC with the roadmap and paste the sysfs helper when ready. Please drop short bullets in the PR as you spike. :rocket:
